# Independent review

Read this when preparing or judging the Phase 3 review. The entrypoint owns the shared authority,
evidence, and phase-exit rules.

## Seed the gate

Spawn the typed `save-toolkit-reviewer` agent with:

- the mission and threat model from the environment card;
- the pinned contract artifact whose served shapes and error cases must be checked;
- only the focus files from builders' `Check first` packet entries.

Do not seed the reviewer with your diagnosis or proposed fix. If you already suspect a defect,
record it in the orchestrator-owned plan, let the reviewer report independently, and reconcile
afterward. A reviewer given the hypothesis can echo it without demonstrating discovery.

## Judge the result

Read the independent P0/P1 count in context. Zero P0/P1 findings on clean work is valid; findings
are not a quota. Judge coverage instead: dimensions reviewed, threat-model paths inspected,
evidence cited, and scope skipped. A review limited to seeded suspicions or a narrow file list has
not independently exercised the broader candidate, whatever its finding count.

Reviews are read-only. Run them concurrently with the next independent build phase; when a phase
depends on the reviewed code, wait. Safety-critical code always treats review as a gate. Anything
network-exposed or auth-bearing receives explicit security coverage before deploy artifacts ship.

Route P0/P1 fixes to the builder who owns the files. Report P2/P3 findings to the user rather than
silently applying them. Reconcile builder pushback using cited evidence, not rank. A contested
safety-critical finding returns through independent review once; if it remains contested, escalate
both evidence packets to the user and stop the loop.

The gate keys on the file, not diff size. Any later edit to a safety-critical file re-enters review,
including a one-line correction.
